flags.statement: But the general triumph of that method would mean an enormous change in the 'temperament' of philosophy.
flags.reason: the source reads "in what I called in my last lecture the 'temperament' of philosophy." The trimmed words are only the author's own back-reference, so the cut is acceptable. The quoted "temperament" is left unexplained, but nothing argumentative is lost.

flags.statement: The universe has always appeared to the natural mind…
flags.reason: the source begins "So the universe…", and the dropped "So" tied the claim to the preceding Solomon and magic illustration. That is a story tie, and it is a minor cut.

other.text: Neither line is a real fault: the first trim carries only the author's back-reference and the second only a story tie. I count both as pass.
